name: audience-tool-reliability
notes: Supersedes v1, which had a design flaw worth naming: each scenario ran the SAME prompt eight times. That measures the reliability of one specific question deeply, not the reliability of the condition it was meant to represent. v1's AUD-C came back 8/8 and was read as 'multi-iteration turns fire reliably' - a generalization from a single instance. v2 keeps the same 24-message budget but distributes it across four different prompts per condition at two runs each, sampling the condition rather than one member of it. The trade is real and deliberate: per-prompt confidence drops (a single prompt showing 1/2 means little on its own), condition-level confidence rises. That is the right trade when the question is about the condition. Also varies audience signal within each condition - recruiter-shaped, engineer-shaped, PM-shaped, neutral - which v1 held constant without meaning to, making persona a third untested variable.
